title: Today marks a new chapter for Windows, as we bring unmetered intelligence to every desk and every home, and make every PC a place where agents can work securely on your behalf. [Read more]
summary: Today marks a new chapter for Windows, as we bring unmetered intelligence to every desk and every home, and make every PC a place where agents can work securely on your behalf. Some highlights of what we announced: • MAI-Code-1.1 Flash: 137B parameter coding model w/ 256K context window, which is now optimized to run on your PC! • GitHub Copilot now hands off work to local models like MAI-Code-1.1 Flash, helping projects cost a lot less without sacrificing quality. • With Hybrid Intelligence, Copilot can now take action directly on the PC and keep sensitive work on your device. • And with Code in Copilot, you can essentially build any software you need on your desktop, without any cloud token spend, and it’s just super at it. You’re no longer limited to what’s in an app store! Your PC becomes an infinite software factory. • Security is foundational to all this, which is why we are also bringing together Windows and Agent 365 so agents can work within secure boundaries on-device, including MXC a local sandbox for agent execution. Windows becomes your secure agent box! • All this comes to life on a new generation of devices, like Surface Laptop Ultra, powered by NVIDIA RTX Spark. Can’t wait to see what you build with all this. Read more about what we announced: https://lnkd.in/gFaRcv_X | 752 comments on LinkedIn

[Satya Nadella](https://www.linkedin.com/in/satyanadella?trk=public_post_feed-actor-name) Satya Nadella is an Influencer

Today marks a new chapter for Windows, as we bring unmetered intelligence to every desk and every home, and make every PC a place where agents can work securely on your behalf. Some highlights of what we announced: • MAI-Code-1.1 Flash: 137B parameter coding model w/ 256K context window, which is now optimized to run on your PC! • GitHub Copilot now hands off work to local models like MAI-Code-1.1 Flash, helping projects cost a lot less without sacrificing quality. • With Hybrid Intelligence, Copilot can now take action directly on the PC and keep sensitive work on your device. • And with Code in Copilot, you can essentially build any software you need on your desktop, without any cloud token spend, and it’s just super at it. You’re no longer limited to what’s in an app store! Your PC becomes an infinite software factory. • Security is foundational to all this, which is why we are also bringing together Windows and Agent 365 so agents can work within secure boundaries on-device, including MXC a local sandbox for agent execution. Windows becomes your secure agent box! • All this comes to life on a new generation of devices, like Surface Laptop Ultra, powered by NVIDIA RTX Spark. Can’t wait to see what you build with all this. Read more about what we announced:[https://lnkd.in/gFaRcv_X](https://lnkd.in/gFaRcv_X?trk=public_post-text)

I am puzzled by this direction. Instead of focusing on building a reliable operating system, the emphasis seems to be on adding more AI features. If you listened to users, youd likely find that many people simply want an OS that is stable, efficient, and gets the job done. Not everyone wants an agentic operating system. One of Microsofts core values is diversity. That should include diversity of user preferences as well. Some users want AI deeply integrated into their workflow, while others prefer a simpler, distraction-free experience. Why not offer both? An AI-first, agentic version for those who want it, and a streamlined productivity-focused version for everyone else. Giving users a choice would be the most inclusive approach.

Lowering cloud token costs cannot come at the expense of auditability and governance defensibility. Microsoft’s own 2026 Digital Defense Report emphasizes that AI attacks now compress intrusion-to-impact timelines from days to minutes, while overreliance on Human-in-the-Loop controls introduces systemic oversight failure. Deploying trillion-parameter models and autonomous token factories directly onto endpoint silicon decentralizes execution into local memory—stripping away central visibility and granting persistent, high-privilege access to the device. 🛑 Cost efficiency is meaningless if the resulting execution architecture is not board defensible.

Satya — this is where the governance problem becomes much more concrete. Once agents can act locally, continuously, and across files, applications, credentials, and software on behalf of a user, the question is no longer just whether the sandbox is secure. It is: does the authority for this exact action still stand now? A local agent may still have capability after consent changes, policy changes, account state changes, or the underlying evidence moves. So secure execution needs two distinct layers: can the agent execute safely? is the agent still legitimately authorized to execute this consequence now? The first is containment. The second is Temporal Standing. As PCs become agent execution environments, both are going to matter.
